subject: Emotions
title: The Shortest Emotion
description: A fast breakdown of The Shortest Emotion for builders.

hook.text: Surprise lasts less than a second. It's the shortest of all human emotions—a flash before feelings decide.

buildup.text: Paul Ekman found surprise is universal: every culture makes the same wide-eyed, open-mouthed face.

discovery.text: Surprise isn't positive or negative. It's a blank slate that amplifies whatever emotion comes next.

twist.text: This is why surprise parties can backfire. The jolt amplifies anxiety in some people, not joy.

climax.text: Surprise is the brain's reset button. It forces you to stop, update your model, and pay attention.

punchline.text: Surprise doesn't pick sides. It just turns up the volume.

quiz.question: What is unique about surprise as an emotion?
